name: Maruti Suzuki India Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest passenger-vehicle maker (about 40% domestic PV share in H1 FY27 per Moneycontrol, 2026-10-16) with ~2.1 lakh domestic and ~50,000 export units a month (Oct 2026). Portfolio spans small cars, hatchbacks, CNG and hybrids and a growing SUV range; ~40% of sales are CNG. Majority-owned by Suzuki Motor Corp (~58.7% promoter holding). Exports to Japan, Europe, Africa, LatAm and the Middle East ~18% of volume. Carries a large cash and treasury portfolio (other income Rs 4.2k cr TTM), so equity value is less levered to operating swings than margins suggest, but treasury MTM now adds volatility.

revenue_mix.geography: Japan, Europe, Africa, LatAm, Middle East

cost_structure.note: 79.9% of net sales in Q2 FY27 (company)

exposures.mechanism: Steel ~14% of sales (model estimate, not disclosed). +7% -> cost +0.98% of sales; EBITDA margin ~9-10% (Q2 FY27 9%) -> EBITDA -10% before pass-through; ~50% recovered via price hikes/mix over 1-2 qtrs -> -5%; EV/MCap ~0.9 (large treasury); persistence 0.4 -> -5*0.9*0.4 = -1.8, rounded -2.0. Pack empirical F_STEEL_GLOBAL -0.70 per +10% global HRC (t -1.1): same sign, consistent in size.

evidence.note: Raw material 79.9% of net sales in Q2 vs 75.7% a year earlier; management cites adverse commodity prices (West Asia conflict)
Elevated steel and copper prices squeezing Indian automakers; brokerages trimmed estimates

exposures.mechanism: Direct (not via steel/rubber/INR which have own edges): oil-linked plastics, paints, lubricants, logistics ~8% of sales with ~25% pass-through to price per +10% Brent -> +0.2% of sales cost -> EBITDA -2.2% pre pass-through; plus fuel-cost hit to ownership cost/sentiment (CNG ~40% of Oct 2026 volumes, CNG price tied to gas/crude). Net ~ -1.2 after 50% pass-through, EV 0.9, persistence 0.4 plus demand effect. Agrees with pack empirical -0.99 per +10% (t -2.5).

evidence.note: Margin hit attributed to West Asia conflict commodity inflation
CNG vehicles ~87,000 units, ~40% of Oct 2026 sales; CNG capacity constrained

exposures.mechanism: Tyres/rubber parts ~2.5% of sales. +10% natural/synthetic rubber -> cost +0.25% of sales -> EBITDA -2.5%; 50% recovered -> -1.25%; x0.9 x0.4 = -0.45. Rubber RSS4 is +62% y/y (Mint 2026-11-05), so a large part is already in Q2 numbers.

evidence.note: RSS4 rubber Rs300/kg, +62% vs Nov 2025; tyre makers raising prices

exposures.mechanism: Aluminium (castings, wheels, engine parts) ~3% of sales (estimate). +10% -> 0.3% of sales -> EBITDA -3% pre; 50% passed on; x0.9 x0.4 = -0.54. LME aluminium is -19.6% since 2026-06-01 (factor_state), so currently a tailwind into H2 FY27.

Copper (wiring harness, motors) ~1.3% of sales (estimate). +10% -> 0.13% of sales -> EBITDA -1.3% pre; 50% passed; x0.9 x0.4 = -0.23, rounded -0.3. Pack empirical copper +0.52 (t 0.7) is insignificant and opposite in sign (copper proxies global growth).

evidence.note: Copper cited among elevated raw materials for automakers

exposures.mechanism: Net effect ambiguous. Imports of parts/yen-linked content ~12% of sales vs exports ~15% of sales (Oct 2026 exports 49,872 units = 18% of volume). +3% INR weakness: import cost +0.36% of sales (-3.6% EBITDA) vs export realisation +0.45% (partly offset by local content ~80%) -> small net negative; company named 'adverse foreign exchange movement' in Q2 and MTM losses on treasury. Pack empirical +0.88 (t 0.8) is insignificant/opposite sign; wide range.

evidence.note: Margin pressure from adverse FX movement and MTM losses on invested surplus
Exports up ~60% y/y to 49,872 units in Oct 2026

exposures.mechanism: ~75-80% of cars financed (model knowledge). RBI hiked repo +25bp to 5.50% on 2026-10-07 and moved to 'calibrated tightening'. +25bp -> EMI ~+0.9% -> volume -0.45% (elasticity ~-0.5) -> EBITDA -0.45%*2.5 operating gearing = -1.1%; x0.9 x0.5 = -0.5, plus ~-0.4 from equity multiple compression on a rate-sensitive consumer name = -0.9.

evidence.note: Repo hiked 25bp to 5.50%, stance calibrated tightening; cuts off the table near term

exposures.mechanism: Domestic ~82% of volumes (exports ~18%). +10% industry volumes -> Maruti volume +10% x0.82; contribution margin ~25% of sales vs EBITDA margin ~10% -> operating gearing 2.5x -> EBITDA +20%; x0.9 EV/MCap x persistence 0.3 (cyclical, GST tailwind fading) = +5.5. Oct 2026 industry record >5 lakh units; Maruti order book 2.45 lakh units, network stock 12 days.

evidence.note: Industry sales 5.25-5.30 lakh in Oct 2026; MSIL 2.76 lakh (+25%), pending bookings 2.45 lakh, stock 12 days

exposures.mechanism: Entry/small cars are the rural-heavy part of the range: small cars +38% y/y in Oct 2026 (40,646 units). +5pp rural income/consumption growth -> ~+2% Maruti volume -> EBITDA +5% x0.9 x0.3 = +1.3. Partially overlaps F_AUTO_DEMAND_IN via backbone edge; weight deliberately small.

evidence.note: Small car sales +38% y/y to 40,646 units in Oct 2026

exposures.mechanism: GST 2.0 (Sept 2025) cut small-car GST to 18%; H1 FY27 volumes +27% in Q2 'aided by GST-led demand'. A further broad cut (+1 SSU, 2-5pp) would lift volume ~3-4% (price elasticity ~-1) and EBITDA ~+9%; x0.9 x0.5 structural = +4. Probability of another car-specific cut in 12m is low; weight is conditional.

evidence.note: Volume growth 27% to 6.97 lakh in Q2 'aided by GST-led demand momentum and a low base'

exposures.mechanism: Maruti is an ICE/CNG/hybrid-heavy incumbent with a late EV launch; stronger EV push (incentives, mandates) shifts mix to rivals (TMPV EV mix ~20-23%, M&M BEV). +1 SSU -> ~-1.5% share erosion over time -> EBITDA -4% x0.9 x0.5 structural = -1.8, but partly offset by Maruti's own eVitara/export EV programme and PLI eligibility -> -0.8.

evidence.note: Tata Motors PV gaining share with EV mix 20%+ (Q1 FY27 call)

exposures.mechanism: A tightening (+1) = chip/ECU supply disruption cutting production ~5% for a quarter (as in 2021-22 and the Oct-2025 Nexperia episode - model knowledge). 5% volume x 2.5 gearing = -12% EBITDA for one quarter -> annualised -3% x0.9 x... = -3. No current disruption reported in sourced material.

evidence.note: Not sourced to a 2026 article; historical analogue

exposures.mechanism: Direct channel only (commodity/FX/rate channels are on other edges): Middle East/GCC is a significant export region for Indian-made cars and shipping disruption raises freight; +1 escalation -> export volume -3% on an 18% share = -0.5% volume -> EBITDA -1.3% x0.9 x0.5 = -0.6. Exports nonetheless +60% y/y in Oct 2026, so the realised effect has been small.

current_state.trend: Record volumes (Q2 +27% to 6.97 lakh units; revenue +26% to Rs 53,356 cr) but EBITDA margin down to ~9% from 12% (EBITDA Rs 4,764 cr, -6% y/y) on commodity inflation, FX, MTM losses on treasury and higher depreciation; consolidated PAT Rs 2,466 cr (-26%). Raw material 79.9% of sales vs 75.7%.
current_state.valuation: Price ~Rs 12,600 (2026-11-05); TTM P/E ~29.5x, market cap ~Rs 3.96 lakh cr; stock -33% in CY2026 to an 18-month low in Oct (Business Standard 2026-10-13), +8% in last month.
